Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Spatial Fay-Herriot Model.

Source: R/eblup_sfh.R
eblup_sfh.Rd

This function gives the Spatial Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (EBLUP) or Empirical Best (EB) predictor under normality based on a Fay-Herriot model.

Usage

eblup_sfh(
  formula,
  vardir,
  domain = NULL,
  data,
  method = c("REML", "ML"),
  mse_type = c("analytical", "pbmse", "npbmse", "none"),
  W = NULL,
  B = 100,
  n_threads = 1,
  seed = -1,
  maxiter = 100,
  precision = 1e-04,
  self_benchmark = FALSE,
  benchmark_weight = NULL,
  benchmark_target = NULL,
  benchmark_group = NULL,
  print_result = TRUE,
  mse_method = lifecycle::deprecated()
)

Arguments

formula

an object of class formula that contains a description of the model to be fitted. The variables included in the formula must be contained in the data.

vardir

sampling variances of the direct estimates: a numeric vector, the name of a column of data or a one-sided formula (e.g. ~vardir).

domain

vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing a domain names column in data. If NULL, the domains are numbered consecutively.

data

a data frame or a data frame extension (e.g. a tibble).

method

Fitting method can be chosen between 'ML' and 'REML'.

mse_type

MSE estimator: "analytical" (default), "pbmse" (parametric bootstrap), "npbmse" (nonparametric bootstrap) or "none" (no MSE; mse and rse are NA). When there are unsampled domains, "pbmse"/"npbmse" bootstrap MSE is only defined for the sampled domains; unsampled domains automatically get a full-spatial synthetic (kriging) prediction and analytical MSE merged into the result.

W

A square matrix with dimension equal to the TOTAL number of domains in data (including any unsampled domains where the response is NA). It should contain the row-standardized spatial weights (proximities) between ALL domains, with values ranging from 0 to 1. Rows and columns must be ordered consistently with the domain identifiers in data. Do NOT pre-subset W to sampled domains only – unsampled domains' spatial MSE/ prediction relies on their relation (in W) to sampled neighbors.

B

Number of bootstrap replications when mse_type = "pbmse" or "npbmse".

n_threads

Number of threads used in parallel computation (default 1). Values less than or equal to 0 use all available cores.

seed

Integer seed for bootstrap resampling; -1 (default) sets no seed. A fixed seed does not change the random number stream of the session.

maxiter

maximum number of iterations allowed in the Fisher-scoring algorithm. Default is 100 iterations.

precision

convergence tolerance limit for the Fisher-scoring algorithm. Default value is 0.0001.

self_benchmark

Logical. If TRUE, fits a self-benchmarking model via the augmented model approach (Wang, Fuller, and Qu, 2008; Rao and Molina, 2015, Sec 10.5.1), ensuring that the weighted aggregate of small area estimates automatically matches the direct survey aggregate or specified benchmark targets without post-hoc adjustment.

benchmark_weight

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the domain benchmarking weights in data (e.g. population sizes or shares). Defaults to equal weights.

benchmark_target

Optional numeric scalar or named vector specifying fixed aggregate benchmark target(s). If NULL (default), calibrates to the weighted aggregate of the direct estimates.

benchmark_group

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the grouping / stratum column in data (e.g. province) for group-specific self-benchmarking.

print_result

print coefficient or not, default value is TRUE.

mse_method

Deprecated (fastsae 1.0.0); use mse_type.

Value

The function returns a list with the following objects: estcoef a data frame with the estimated model coefficients (beta), their asymptotic standard errors (std.error, repeated as stderr_beta for compatibility with fastsae 0.1.0), the z-statistics (zvalue) and the normal p-values (pvalue)
random_effect_var estimated random effect variance
rho estimated spatial autocorrelation parameter
estvarcomp a data frame with parameter, estimate, and std.error
goodness named vector: loglikelihood (the full Gaussian log-likelihood at the estimates, for ML and REML fits alike), AIC and BIC computed from it, as sae does and as in Marhuenda, Morales and Pardo (2014). The restricted (REML) likelihood is not reported: it depends on the covariates through X, so it cannot compare models with different covariates.
df_eblup a data frame with one row per domain:

  • domain domain identifier

  • y direct estimate (NA for unsampled domains)

  • eblup estimated results for each area

  • random_effect random effect for each area

  • vardir sampling variance of the direct estimate

  • mse Mean Square Error (the bootstrap MSE for "pbmse"/"npbmse")

  • rse Relative Standard Error (%)

  • mse_pb or mse_npb Parametric / Non Parametric bootstrap MSE

  • mse_pbbc or mse_npbbc Bias Corrected Parametric / Non Parametric bootstrap MSE
    convergence, n_iter whether the fit converged, and its iterations,
    model, method, mse_type, formula, call, data, W the settings, the matched call, the data and the weight matrix used.

Details

The spatial Fay-Herriot model (Petrucci and Salvati, 2006; Pratesi and Salvati, 2008) is \(y = X\beta + u + e\) with a simultaneous autoregressive area effect \(u = \rho W u + \varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I)\), and sampling errors \(e \sim N(0, \mathrm{diag}(\psi_d))\) with known \(\psi_d\) (vardir). When the response is NA, that domain is treated as unsampled: it is predicted with a full-spatial synthetic (kriging) estimator that borrows strength from sampled neighbors via W. The SAR process is defined on all domains of W, so the sampled domains have covariance \(\sigma^2 \Sigma[s,s]\) with \(\Sigma = [(I - \rho W')(I - \rho W)]^{-1}\).

An estimate \(\hat\sigma^2 = 0\) makes the EBLUPs synthetic estimates, and the MSE estimates can then understate the error; the function says so with a message (see Li and Lahiri, 2010).

Analytical MSE. Sampled domains: \(g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 - g_4\) (Singh et al., 2005; as sae::mseSFH; the bootstrap MSEs are those of Molina et al., 2009), minus \(b_{ML}'\nabla g_1\) for ML. Unsampled domains: \(g_1 + g_2 + g_3 - \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(I^{-1}\nabla^2 g_1)\) (minus \(b_{ML}'\nabla g_1\) for ML), with \(g_3\) from the exact derivative of the kriging predictor; for sampled domains this second-order form agrees, up to o(1/m), with \(g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 - g_4\). The inverse information used for \(g_3\) and \(b_{ML}\) is the one of the fitting method: REML information for REML and ML information for ML. (sae::mseSFH uses the REML information also for ML; the two agree asymptotically, but with few domains, or \(\hat\sigma^2 \approx 0\) with \(\hat\rho \approx 1\), the REML choice can make the ML bias term explode. Hence, for method = "ML", the MSE differs from sae::mseSFH; REML results agree.)

When \(\hat\rho\) lies on the boundary (\(|\hat\rho| \ge 0.999\), or reported as \(-1\)), the Prasad-Rao expansion in \(\rho\) is not valid and can explode, so \(\rho\) is treated as fixed: only the \(\sigma^2\) block of the information is inverted, which removes the \(\rho\) terms from \(g_3\), \(g_4\) and \(b_{ML}\) (the standard error of \(\rho\) is then NA). In this case the MSE differs from sae::mseSFH, which keeps those terms.

If the classical (sae-compatible) Fisher scoring fails, or converges to a negative \(\sigma^2\) (which sae::eblupSFH truncates to 0 without re-estimating \(\rho\)), the (RE)ML likelihood is maximised under the constraints \(\sigma^2 \ge 0\), \(|\rho| \le 0.999\). A lower-bound estimate \(\rho = -0.999\) is reported as \(-1\) (as sae) only when \(I + W\) is non-singular (not for bipartite graphs such as a rook grid).

Computation. No \(D \times D\) inverse is formed: with \(A = (I - \rho W')(I - \rho W)\) and \(M = A + \sigma^2 E'\Psi^{-1}E\) (\(E\) selects the sampled domains), \(V^{-1} = \Psi^{-1} - \sigma^2\Psi^{-1}EM^{-1}E'\Psi^{-1}\), \(g_1 = \sigma^2\,\mathrm{diag}(M^{-1})\) and the remaining terms follow from Cholesky solves with \(A\) and \(M\). These are sparse for a sparse W (contiguity or k-nearest-neighbour weights), which makes models with a few thousand domains feasible; a dense W (e.g. inverse-distance weights) uses dense factorisations.

References

  1. Li, H., and Lahiri, P. (2010). An adjusted maximum likelihood method for solving small area estimation problems. Journal of Multivariate Analysis, 101(4), 882-892.

  2. Marhuenda, Y., Morales, D., & Pardo, M. C. (2014). Information criteria for Fay-Herriot model selection. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 70, 268-280.

  3. Molina, I., Salvati, N., & Pratesi, M. (2009). Bootstrap for estimating the MSE of the spatial EBLUP. Computational Statistics, 24(3), 441-458.

  4. Petrucci, A., & Salvati, N. (2006). Small area estimation for spatial correlation in watershed erosion assessment. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 11(2), 169-182.

  5. Pratesi, M., & Salvati, N. (2008). Small area estimation: the EBLUP estimator based on spatially correlated random area effects. Statistical Methods & Applications, 17(1), 113-141.

  6. Rao, J. N., & Molina, I. (2015). Small area estimation. John Wiley & Sons.

  7. Singh, B. B., Shukla, G. K., & Kundu, D. (2005). Spatio-temporal models in small area estimation. Survey Methodology, 31(2), 183-195.

See also

eblup_fh, eblup_stfh for repeated surveys, spatial_test to check whether a spatial model is needed, create_weights to build W.

Examples

library(fastsae)

# Spatial Fay-Herriot model
m1 <- eblup_sfh(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
  data = mys,
  vardir = ~vardir,
  W = mys_proxmat
)
#>

# Spatial Fay-Herriot model with Parametric Bootstrap MSE
m2 <- eblup_sfh(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
  data = mys,
  vardir = ~vardir,
  mse_type = "pbmse",
  B = 50,
  W = mys_proxmat
)
